post.title: REA: Reverse Engineer Anything
post.hook: One MCP server to take apart binaries, Electron apps, APKs and websites.
post.summary: REA is an MCP server and CLI that lets an agent inspect native binaries, JavaScript apps, Android APKs and more, returning findings with evidence. It has shipped many releases, with 2,493 commits from 202 authors.
post.writeup:
## What it is
REA (Reverse Engineer Anything) is an MCP server and CLI for reverse engineering. An agent points it at a local target and gets back findings with the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion. Analysis runs locally.

## Why it exists
The pitch: see a feature in an app you like, understand how it works down to the binary level, then have your agent build a version for your own project.

## How it works
`npx rea-agents setup` registers the MCP server with agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI, and installs matching workflow instructions. The agent calls REA to inspect the target and trace code. It then uses the returned code, references and unknowns to explain, implement and test. The same workflows are available as terminal commands.

## What it covers
The README table lists 14 target types: native binaries (via Hopper, Ghidra or IDA), ELF layout, Go binaries, WASM, EVM bytecode, SQLite databases, recorded Linux crashes, JavaScript and Electron, websites, saved network captures, .NET assemblies, Android APKs, Android devices and JEB projects.

## Progress
The repo started on 2026-04-14 as a Hopper Disassembler MCP server. Most activity came later: 1418 commits in the week of 2026-10-05 alone. Release 6.4.0 (2026-10-11) added ADB device inspection, JEB project browsing, Ghidra import options and tRPC and GraphQL discovery. The website is plain HTML and CSS with translated editions, and the README exists in 19 languages.

## Open questions
Native analysis depends on a separately installed engine, and several targets need extra tools such as pwntools, WABT or JADX. How much of that setup can be automated is still open.

slides.heading: What REA can analyze
rows: Pseudocode, assembly, strings, symbols, calls and references
Embedded compiler version, modules, replacements and build settings
Dispatch selectors, byte offsets, inferred arguments and mutability
Modules, imports, source maps, routes, IPC and native add-on relationships
Manifest declarations, classes, decompiled methods and references
Engine-backed project units, artifact digests and type/method pseudo-code
